    <text x="150" y="240" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="14" fill="#64748B">Models can decompose complex multi-step</text>
    <text x="150" y="260" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="14" fill="#64748B">problems into coherent solution plans,</text>
    <text x="150" y="280" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="14" fill="#64748B">enabling longer chains of autonomous work.</text>

    <!-- Card 2: Better Tool Use -->
    <rect x="665" y="170" width="555" height="170" fill="#F8FAFC" stroke="#E2E8F0" stroke-width="1" rx="10" filter="url(#softShadow)"/>
    <rect x="665" y="170" width="555" height="5" fill="#4A90D9" rx="3"/>
    <circle cx="710" cy="220" r="28" fill="#4A90D9" fill-opacity="0.1"/>
    <use data-icon="wrench" x="688" y="198" width="44" height="44" fill="#4A90D9"/>
    <text x="755" y="214" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="18" font-weight="bold" fill="#1E293B">Better Tool Use</text>
    <text x="755" y="240" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="14" fill="#64748B">Effective use of shells, APIs, file systems,</text>
    <text x="755" y="260" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="14" fill="#64748B">and development tools — the scaffolding for</text>
    <text x="755" y="280" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="14" fill="#64748B">extended autonomous software tasks.</text>

    <!-- Card 3: Reliability & Self-Awareness -->
    <rect x="60" y="360" width="555" height="170" fill="#F8FAFC" stroke="#E2E8F0" stroke-width="1" rx="10" filter="url(#softShadow)"/>
    <rect x="60" y="360" width="555" height="5" fill="#D97757" rx="3"/>
    <circle cx="105" cy="410" r="28" fill="#D97757" fill-opacity="0.1"/>
    <use data-icon="shield-check" x="83" y="388" width="44" height="44" fill="#D97757"/>
    <text x="150" y="404" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="18" font-weight="bold" fill="#1E293B">Greater Reliability & Self-Awareness</text>
    <text x="150" y="430" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="14" fill="#64748B">Models better recognize when they are stuck</text>
    <text x="150" y="450" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="14" fill="#64748B">or producing incorrect output, reducing</text>
    <text x="150" y="470" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="14" fill="#64748B">compounding errors over long task horizons.</text>

    <!-- Card 4: Error Recovery -->
    <rect x="665" y="360" width="555" height="170" fill="#F8FAFC" stroke="#E2E8F0" stroke-width="1" rx="10" filter="url(#softShadow)"/>
    <rect x="665" y="360" width="555" height="5" fill="#10B981" rx="3"/>
    <circle cx="710" cy="410" r="28" fill="#10B981" fill-opacity="0.1"/>
    <use data-icon="arrow-rotate-right" x="688" y="388" width="44" height="44" fill="#10B981"/>
    <text x="755" y="404" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="18" font-weight="bold" fill="#1E293B">Ability to Adapt to Mistakes</text>
    <text x="755" y="430" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="14" fill="#64748B">When encountering errors or unexpected</text>
    <text x="755" y="450" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="14" fill="#64748B">results, frontier models can diagnose and</text>
    <text x="755" y="470" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="14" fill="#64748B">correct course — critical for longer tasks.</text>

    <!-- Limitation callout -->
    <rect x="60" y="555" width="1160" height="80" fill="#EF4444" fill-opacity="0.05" stroke="#EF4444" stroke-opacity="0.2" stroke-width="1" rx="8"/>
    <use data-icon="triangle-exclamation" x="80" y="574" width="32" height="32" fill="#EF4444"/>
    <text x="125" y="590" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="16" font-weight="bold" fill="#EF4444">Key Limitation</text>
    <text x="125" y="614" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="14" fill="#64748B">Performance is notably lower on less structured, "messier" tasks. External validity remains an open question — the task suite</text>
    <text x="125" y="632" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="14" fill="#64748B">does not perfectly represent the average segment of real-world intellectual labor.</text>

    <!-- Page number -->
    <text x="640" y="705" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="12" fill="#94A3B8" text-anchor="middle">6 / 8</text>
</svg>

    <circle cx="100" cy="216" r="18" fill="#10B981" fill-opacity="0.15"/>

    <text x="1100" y="410" text-anchor="end" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="20" font-weight="bold" fill="#4A90D9">~2 hrs</text>

    <circle cx="100" cy="501" r="18" fill="#F59E0B" fill-opacity="0.15"/>
    <text x="100" y="507" text-anchor="middle" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="14" font-weight="bold" fill="#F59E0B">4</text>
    <text x="135" y="492" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="16" font-weight="bold" fill="#FFFFFF">External Validity Remains an Open Question</text>
    <text x="135" y="515" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="14" fill="#FFFFFF" fill-opacity="0.7">Tasks may not perfectly represent real-world intellectual labor distributions — but supplementary experiments</text>
    <text x="135" y="535" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="14" fill="#FFFFFF" fill-opacity="0.7">found little evidence that trends are slower on more realistic tasks.</text>

    <!-- Takeaway 5 -->
    <rect x="60" y="555" width="1160" height="82" fill="#FFFFFF" fill-opacity="0.04" stroke="#FFFFFF" stroke-opacity="0.08" stroke-width="1" rx="8"/>
    <circle cx="100" cy="596" r="18" fill="#EF4444" fill-opacity="0.15"/>
    <text x="100" y="602" text-anchor="middle" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="14" font-weight="bold" fill="#EF4444">5</text>
    <text x="135" y="587" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="16" font-weight="bold" fill="#FFFFFF">Key Limitations: Unstructured Tasks & Uncertain Generalization</text>
    <text x="135" y="610" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="14" fill="#FFFFFF" fill-opacity="0.7">Performance is notably lower on "messier" tasks. Generalization to real-world job distributions uncertain.</text>
    <text x="135" y="630" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="14" fill="#FFFFFF" fill-opacity="0.7">Safety governance frameworks must account for both the trend and its uncertainty bounds.</text>

    <!-- Bottom separator -->
    <rect x="60" y="655" width="1160" height="1" fill="#FFFFFF" fill-opacity="0.1"/>
    <text x="60" y="690" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="12" fill="#64748B">Source: Kwa et al. (2025) — METR</text>
    <text x="1220" y="690" text-anchor="end" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="12" fill="#64748B">8 / 8</text>
</svg>

    <!-- Glow -->
    <ellipse cx="640" cy="100" rx="400" ry="150" fill="url(#glowOrange)"/>

    <!-- Page label -->
    <text x="60" y="50" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="13" font-weight="500" fill="#D97757" letter-spacing="2">KEY TAKEAWAYS</text>

    <!-- Title -->
    <text x="60" y="95" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="28" font-weight="bold" fill="#FFFFFF">
        Exponential Autonomous Capability Growth
    </text>
    <text x="60" y="130" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="28" font-weight="bold" fill="#FFFFFF">
        Demands Proactive Safety Governance
    </text>

    <!-- Separator -->
    <rect x="60" y="148" width="160" height="3" fill="url(#accentGradient)" rx="1.5"/>

    <!-- Takeaway 1 -->
    <rect x="60" y="175" width="1160" height="82" fill="#FFFFFF" fill-opacity="0.04" stroke="#FFFFFF" stroke-opacity="0.08" stroke-width="1" rx="8"/>
    <circle cx="100" cy="216" r="18" fill="#10B981" fill-opacity="0.15"/>
    <text x="100" y="222" text-anchor="middle" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="14" font-weight="bold" fill="#10B981">1</text>
    <text x="135" y="207" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="16" font-weight="bold" fill="#FFFFFF">Robust, Intuitive Metric</text>
    <text x="135" y="230" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="14" fill="#FFFFFF" fill-opacity="0.7">50% time horizon provides a single number for tracking AI autonomous capability growth.</text>
    <text x="1100" y="220" text-anchor="end" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="20" font-weight="bold" fill="#10B981">R² = 0.97</text>
    <text x="1100" y="240" text-anchor="end" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="12" fill="#64748B">over 6 years</text>

    <!-- Takeaway 2 -->
    <rect x="60" y="270" width="1160" height="82" fill="#FFFFFF" fill-opacity="0.04" stroke="#FFFFFF" stroke-opacity="0.08" stroke-width="1" rx="8"/>
    <circle cx="100" cy="311" r="18" fill="#D97757" fill-opacity="0.15"/>
    <text x="100" y="317" text-anchor="middle" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="14" font-weight="bold" fill="#D97757">2</text>
    <text x="135" y="302" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="16" font-weight="bold" fill="#FFFFFF">Rapid Doubling with Possible Acceleration</text>
    <text x="135" y="325" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="14" fill="#FFFFFF" fill-opacity="0.7">Doubling every ~7 months. The 2023–2025 rate is ~20% faster than the overall 2019–2025 trend.</text>
    <text x="1100" y="315" text-anchor="end" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="20" font-weight="bold" fill="#D97757">~7 mo</text>
    <text x="1100" y="335" text-anchor="end" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="12" fill="#64748B">doubling time</text>

    <!-- Takeaway 3 -->
    <rect x="60" y="365" width="1160" height="82" fill="#FFFFFF" fill-opacity="0.04" stroke="#FFFFFF" stroke-opacity="0.08" stroke-width="1" rx="8"/>
    <circle cx="100" cy="406" r="18" fill="#4A90D9" fill-opacity="0.15"/>
    <text x="100" y="412" text-anchor="middle" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="14" font-weight="bold" fill="#4A90D9">3</text>
    <text x="135" y="397" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="16" font-weight="bold" fill="#FFFFFF">Current Frontier: ~2 Hours of Human-Equivalent Work</text>
    <text x="135" y="420" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="14" fill="#FFFFFF" fill-opacity="0.7">o3 can autonomously complete tasks that take skilled humans nearly 2 hours — up from 2 seconds for GPT-2.</text>
    <text x="1100" y="410" text-anchor="end" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="20" font-weight="bold" fill="#4A90D9">~2 hrs</text>
    <text x="1100" y="430" text-anchor="end" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="12" fill="#64748B">o3 frontier</text>

    <!-- Takeaway 4 -->
    <rect x="60" y="460" width="1160" height="82" fill="#FFFFFF" fill-opacity="0.04" stroke="#FFFFFF" stroke-opacity="0.08" stroke-width="1" rx="8"/>
    <circle cx="100" cy="501" r="18" fill="#F59E0B" fill-opacity="0.15"/>
    <text x="100" y="507" text-anchor="middle" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="14" font-weight="bold" fill="#F59E0B">4</text>
    <text x="135" y="492" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="16" font-weight="bold" fill="#FFFFFF">External Validity Remains an Open Question</text>
    <text x="135" y="515" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="14" fill="#FFFFFF" fill-opacity="0.7">Tasks may not perfectly represent real-world intellectual labor distributions — but supplementary experiments</text>
    <text x="135" y="535" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="14" fill="#FFFFFF" fill-opacity="0.7">found little evidence that trends are slower on more realistic tasks.</text>

    <!-- Takeaway 5 -->
    <rect x="60" y="555" width="1160" height="82" fill="#FFFFFF" fill-opacity="0.04" stroke="#FFFFFF" stroke-opacity="0.08" stroke-width="1" rx="8"/>
    <circle cx="100" cy="596" r="18" fill="#EF4444" fill-opacity="0.15"/>
    <text x="100" y="602" text-anchor="middle" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="14" font-weight="bold" fill="#EF4444">5</text>
    <text x="135" y="587" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="16" font-weight="bold" fill="#FFFFFF">Key Limitations: Unstructured Tasks & Uncertain Generalization</text>
    <text x="135" y="610" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="14" fill="#FFFFFF" fill-opacity="0.7">Performance is notably lower on "messier" tasks. Generalization to real-world job distributions uncertain.</text>
    <text x="135" y="630" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="14" fill="#FFFFFF" fill-opacity="0.7">Safety governance frameworks must account for both the trend and its uncertainty bounds.</text>

    <!-- Bottom separator -->
    <rect x="60" y="655" width="1160" height="1" fill="#FFFFFF" fill-opacity="0.1"/>
    <text x="60" y="690" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="12" fill="#64748B">Source: Kwa et al. (2025) — METR</text>
    <text x="1220" y="690" text-anchor="end" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="12" fill="#64748B">8 / 8</text>
</svg>

arguments.content:
# 01_cover

Welcome to this presentation on measuring AI ability to complete long software tasks. This research, published by METR in March 2025, introduces a powerful new metric for tracking autonomous AI capabilities. [Pause]

The headline finding is striking: the 50% task-completion time horizon — the duration of tasks AI can complete with 50% success — has been doubling approximately every 7 months since 2019.

Key points: (1) New metric from METR quantifies autonomous AI capability growth (2) Doubling time of ~7 months with R² = 0.97 (3) Implications span safety, governance, and workforce automation
Duration: 2 minutes

---

# 02_metric_explained

[Transition] Before examining the trend, let's understand how this metric works.

The 50% task-completion time horizon gives us an intuitive, human-grounded measure. The methodology has three steps: first, assemble a diverse suite of 170 software and research tasks. Second, time skilled human professionals and measure AI agent success rates. Third, fit a logistic model to find the task duration at which each AI model achieves 50% success. [Pause]

This approach allows direct comparison across vastly different models — from GPT-2 to o3.

Key points: (1) Three-step methodology: task suite, human timing, logistic fit (2) Human-grounded measure enables cross-model comparison (3) 170 tasks spanning seconds to hours
Duration: 2.5 minutes

---

# 03_task_suite

[Transition] Now let's look at what makes up that 170-task suite.

The benchmark combines three complementary sources. SWAA provides 66 short atomic tasks from 1 to 30 seconds — things like identifying which file is a shell script. HCAST contributes the bulk with 97 diverse software tasks ranging from 1 minute to 30 hours, including bug fixes, data transformation, and simulation debugging. RE-Bench rounds it out with 7 extremely difficult ML research engineering tasks, all taking 8 hours. [Pause]

[Data] The human baseline effort is substantial — over 800 human baselines totaling 2,529 hours of work.

Key points: (1) Three complementary suites: SWAA (short), HCAST (diverse), RE-Bench (hard) (2) Full spectrum from 3 seconds to 8 hours (3) Grounded in 2,529 hours of human baseline work
Duration: 2.5 minutes

---

# 04_exponential_trend

[Transition] With that task suite in hand, here is the central finding of the paper.

The 50% time horizon has grown exponentially from 2019 to 2025. [Pause] Look at the trajectory: GPT-2 in 2019 could handle tasks taking about 2 seconds. GPT-4 in 2023 reached about 5 minutes. And o3, released in early 2025, pushes to approximately 1 hour and 50 minutes. [Data] That's a doubling time of roughly 207 days — about 7 months — with an R² of 0.97. [Pause]

[Benchmark] Notably, the 2023–2025 growth rate is approximately 20% faster than the overall 2019–2025 rate, suggesting possible acceleration.

Key points: (1) Exponential growth from 2s to ~2h in 6 years (2) ~207-day doubling time, R² = 0.97 (3) Possible acceleration since 2023
Duration: 3 minutes

---

# 05_success_curves

[Transition] Let's look at this from another angle — the per-model success probability curves.

Every model shows the same pattern: success probability drops sharply as task length increases. The key difference is where the curve sits. Older models like GPT-2 drop to 50% at just 2 seconds. Frontier models push the curve rightward — Claude 3.7 Sonnet hits 50% at about 54 minutes, and o3 at roughly 1 hour 50 minutes. [Pause]

The 80% time horizon — tasks completed 80% of the time — follows a similar trend but with horizons approximately 5 times shorter, showing that reliability drops faster than capability extends.

Key points: (1) Universal pattern: steep success decline with task length (2) Frontier models shift curve rightward (3) 80% horizon is ~5x shorter than 50% horizon
Duration: 2.5 minutes

---

# 06_drivers

[Transition] What's driving this exponential improvement?

The paper identifies four key capability drivers. First, improved logical reasoning — models can decompose complex multi-step problems into coherent plans. Second, better tool use — effective interaction with shells, APIs, and development tools. Third, greater reliability and self-awareness — recognizing when they're stuck. And fourth, the ability to adapt to mistakes and correct course. [Pause]

[Scan Room] However, there's an important caveat. Performance remains notably lower on less structured, "messier" tasks. External validity is an open question — the task suite doesn't perfectly represent real-world intellectual labor.

Key points: (1) Four drivers: reasoning, tool use, reliability, error recovery (2) Performance lower on unstructured tasks (3) External validity remains uncertain
Duration: 2.5 minutes

---

# 07_extrapolation

[Transition] Now for the forward-looking implications that matter most for this audience.

If the current trend continues — and that's a significant "if" — naive extrapolation predicts AI will reach a 1-month time horizon, meaning 167 work hours, between mid-2028 and mid-2031. [Pause] That would imply automation of many month-long software projects.

The uncertainty range is wide because it depends on whether you use the overall 2019–2025 rate or the faster 2023–2025 rate. [Data] The recent rate is about 20% faster, but exponential trends rarely continue indefinitely. [Pause]

Three key caveats: external validity is uncertain, the trend could change due to architectural shifts or saturation, and supplementary experiments found little evidence that trends are slower on more realistic tasks.

Key points: (1) 1-month horizon projected for 2028–2031 (2) Range reflects uncertainty in growth rate (3) Caveats: validity, trend durability, real-world generalization
Duration: 3 minutes
Flex: [If time is tight, summarize caveats briefly and move to takeaways]

---

# 08_takeaways

[Transition] Let me close with five key takeaways for safety governance.

First, the 50% time horizon is a robust metric — R² of 0.97 over 6 years of model releases. Second, the doubling time is approximately 7 months, with possible acceleration since 2024. Third, the current frontier stands at roughly 2 hours of human-equivalent autonomous work. [Pause]

Fourth, external validity remains open — we should be cautious about direct extrapolation to all intellectual labor. And fifth, key limitations include poor performance on unstructured tasks and uncertain generalization. [Pause]

The strategic implication is clear: exponential growth in autonomous AI capabilities demands proactive safety governance frameworks — not reactive ones.

Key points: (1) Robust metric with clear exponential trend (2) ~7-month doubling with acceleration signals (3) Safety governance must be proactive given the pace
Duration: 2.5 minutes

Key points: (1) Universal pattern: steep success decline with task length (2) Frontier models shift curve rightward (3) 80% horizon is ~5x shorter than 50% horizon
Duration: 2.5 minutes

---

# 06_drivers

[Transition] What's driving this exponential improvement?

The paper identifies four key capability drivers. First, improved logical reasoning — models can decompose complex multi-step problems into coherent plans. Second, better tool use — effective interaction with shells, APIs, and development tools. Third, greater reliability and self-awareness — recognizing when they're stuck. And fourth, the ability to adapt to mistakes and correct course. [Pause]

[Scan Room] However, there's an important caveat. Performance remains notably lower on less structured, "messier" tasks. External validity is an open question — the task suite doesn't perfectly represent real-world intellectual labor.

Key points: (1) Four drivers: reasoning, tool use, reliability, error recovery (2) Performance lower on unstructured tasks (3) External validity remains uncertain
Duration: 2.5 minutes

---

# 07_extrapolation

[Transition] Now for the forward-looking implications that matter most for this audience.

If the current trend continues — and that's a significant "if" — naive extrapolation predicts AI will reach a 1-month time horizon, meaning 167 work hours, between mid-2028 and mid-2031. [Pause] That would imply automation of many month-long software projects.

The uncertainty range is wide because it depends on whether you use the overall 2019–2025 rate or the faster 2023–2025 rate. [Data] The recent rate is about 20% faster, but exponential trends rarely continue indefinitely. [Pause]

Three key caveats: external validity is uncertain, the trend could change due to architectural shifts or saturation, and supplementary experiments found little evidence that trends are slower on more realistic tasks.

Key points: (1) 1-month horizon projected for 2028–2031 (2) Range reflects uncertainty in growth rate (3) Caveats: validity, trend durability, real-world generalization
Duration: 3 minutes
Flex: [If time is tight, summarize caveats briefly and move to takeaways]

---

# 08_takeaways

[Transition] Let me close with five key takeaways for safety governance.

First, the 50% time horizon is a robust metric — R² of 0.97 over 6 years of model releases. Second, the doubling time is approximately 7 months, with possible acceleration since 2024. Third, the current frontier stands at roughly 2 hours of human-equivalent autonomous work. [Pause]

Fourth, external validity remains open — we should be cautious about direct extrapolation to all intellectual labor. And fifth, key limitations include poor performance on unstructured tasks and uncertain generalization. [Pause]

The strategic implication is clear: exponential growth in autonomous AI capabilities demands proactive safety governance frameworks — not reactive ones.

Key points: (1) Robust metric with clear exponential trend (2) ~7-month doubling with acceleration signals (3) Safety governance must be proactive given the pace
Duration: 2.5 minutes
